agree.reason: The $99 trial and no-contract terms make a single booking low-risk, but this reader is happy saving $25 a visit and has no complaint, so the insurance argument alone is unlikely to bring them back at $165.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief, and the email avoids the false 'same cleaner every time' promise; 'You'll always know who's coming' is a little strong, but a named backup supports it.

works_the_facts.reason: It quotes the raw figures but works none of them out: it never puts the $25 gap in a smaller form (about $12 a week), never notes that the $99 first visit costs less than the app, and never turns 1 departure since July into a retention rate set against 7 last year.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the apps truthfully as cheaper and run by uninsured contractors, and it shows the company's own turnover trend improving, but it says nothing about whether app customers get the same cleaner.

qualification.reason: The offer has a clear end date (December 31), a stated price after the first visit, and no contract, so the reader can check every term.

objections.reason: It meets the price objection head-on with what the extra money pays for, but it never says why insurance or employed staff should matter to this particular householder, and it spends space on cleaner turnover, which this reader never complained about.

fit.reason: It is a well-built win-back email with a clear call to action, though at about 170 words it runs somewhat over the requested 150.
